vocabulary.en: behaving in an unpredictable or uncontrolled way

vocabulary.example_cn: 要求在该区域内运行的每架飞机都获得许可。

vocabulary.en: running lengthwise
vocabulary.excerpt: one and a half miles longitudinal or horizontal
vocabulary.example_cn: 纵向或水平方向1.5英里。

vocabulary.en: at right angles to a horizontal plane
vocabulary.excerpt: 500 feet vertical
vocabulary.example_cn: 垂直方向500英尺。

vocabulary.excerpt: creates, maybe, an operational error or less than standard separation.
vocabulary.example_cn: 可能导致操作失误或低于标准的间隔。

vocabulary.en: occurring in the air
vocabulary.excerpt: since the mid-air of about a year and a half ago
vocabulary.example_cn: 自从大约一年半前的空中相撞事件以来。

vocabulary.en: rumor or gossip
vocabulary.excerpt: Like what's the scuttlebutt?
vocabulary.example_cn: 有什么小道消息？

sentences.en: He was outspent, you know, almost 10 to 1.
sentences.cn: 你知道，他的竞选支出被对手以近10比1的比例超过。
sentences.structure: 主语+谓语（被动语态）+状语
sentences.analysis: 被动语态，outspent是outspend的过去分词，表示被超过。

sentences.en: And I think that is actually resonating with -- with Michigan.
sentences.cn: 我认为这实际上正在引起密歇根州的共鸣。
sentences.analysis: think后接宾语从句，resonating with表示引起共鸣。

sentences.cn: 他是一位出色的政治运动员。
sentences.analysis: political athlete是比喻，指擅长政治活动的人。

sentences.cn: 埃尔-萨耶德拒绝与他划清界限。
sentences.analysis: refuse to do sth. 拒绝做某事。

sentences.en: The establishment put all their weight behind trying to crush Abdul in Michigan.
sentences.cn: 当权派全力试图在密歇根州击败阿卜杜勒。
sentences.analysis: put weight behind表示支持或努力推动。

sentences.en: You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of...
sentences.cn: 你们都是令人难以置信的仇视伊斯兰教的家伙。
sentences.analysis: unbelievably修饰形容词，pieces of...是粗俗用语。

sentences.en: I think we tend to oversell how divisive primaries are.
sentences.cn: 我认为我们往往夸大了初选的分裂程度。
sentences.analysis: tend to do sth. 倾向于做某事；oversell意为过度推销。

sentences.en: This kind of rhetoric coming from your supporters, who he was just with two days earlier, really not helpful.
sentences.cn: 这种来自你的支持者的言论，他两天前还和他们在一起，真的没有帮助。
sentences.analysis: coming from...是现在分词短语作定语，who引导非限制性定语从句。

sentences.en: Iran reporting progress in talks with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, saying that the two sides are close to finalizing a proposed framework.
sentences.cn: 伊朗报告称与阿曼就霍尔木兹海峡的谈判取得进展，称双方接近敲定拟议框架。
sentences.analysis: reporting和saying是现在分词作状语，表示伴随动作。

sentences.en: The Trump administration has detained more than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty U.S. troops while pursuing their mass deportation agenda.
sentences.cn: 特朗普政府在推行大规模驱逐议程的同时，拘留了50多名现役美军士兵的父母和配偶。
sentences.structure: 主语+谓语+宾语+时间状语从句
sentences.analysis: while pursuing...是省略主语的时间状语从句，相当于while they are pursuing...。

sentences.en: Edwards abandoned his reelection bid this week after an ethics panel found that he repeatedly made unwanted advances towards two female staffers.
sentences.cn: 爱德华兹本周放弃了连任竞选，此前道德委员会发现他多次对两名女性工作人员进行不受欢迎的挑逗。
sentences.analysis: after引导时间状语从句，found后接宾语从句。

sentences.en: Another day, another A.I. model has now apparently gone rogue.
sentences.cn: 又一天，又一个AI模型显然失控了。
sentences.analysis: gone rogue是固定搭配，意为失控。

sentences.en: The FAA and the NTSB are now reviewing an incident involving Trump's Marine One helicopter and a passenger jet that got too close.
sentences.cn: 美国联邦航空管理局和国家运输安全委员会正在审查一起涉及特朗普的海军陆战队一号直升机与一架客机距离过近的事件。
sentences.structure: 主语+谓语+宾语+定语从句
sentences.analysis: involving...是现在分词短语作定语，that got too close是定语从句修饰passenger jet。

sentences.en: Based on our preliminary safety review, there was a momentary loss of separation after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another.
sentences.cn: 根据我们的初步安全审查，出现了短暂的间隔丧失，之后飞机继续相互远离。
sentences.structure: 状语+there be句型+定语从句
sentences.analysis: after which引导非限制性定语从句，修饰loss of separation。

sentences.en: So, the protocol here is that when the Marine One calls for an indication that he's going to take off, the tower controller stops any departures.
sentences.cn: 所以，这里的协议是，当海军陆战队一号发出即将起飞的指示时，塔台管制员会停止所有离港航班。
sentences.analysis: that引导表语从句，其中包含when引导的时间状语从句和that引导的同位语从句。

sentences.en: And when there is confusion between the pilot and the controller or the controller and the pilot, and they're both not on the same page, that is often -- creates, maybe, an operational error or less than standard separation.
sentences.cn: 当飞行员和管制员之间或管制员和飞行员之间存在困惑，且双方不在同一频道时，这往往会导致操作失误或低于标准的间隔。
sentences.analysis: when引导时间状语从句，主句为that is often...，其中creates是插入语。

raw_transcript:
Return to Transcripts main page

El-Sayed Wins Michigan; FAA Reviewing Incident Involving Trump's Marine One & Passenger Jet. Aired 6-6:30a ET

Aired August 06, 2026 - 06:00   ET

THIS IS A RUSH TRANSCRIPT. THIS COPY MAY NOT BE IN ITS FINAL FORM AND MAY BE UPDATED.

AUDIE CORNISH, CNN ANCHOR: Today in the group chat, President Trump says Abdul El-Sayed's win in Michigan is good news for Republicans. Is he right?

ABDUL EL-SAYED (D), MICHIGAN SENATORIAL CANDIDATE: Democrats worrying is not going to solve the problem.

CORNISH: And a passenger plane got a little too close to President Trump's Marine One while he was on board. How close is too close?

And another tech giant admits that its A.I. model went rogue. How many times does this have to happen before something is done about it?

SEN. RICHARD BLUMENTHAL (D-CT): Blanche again said the quiet part out loud. In fact, he shouted it.

CORNISH: Attorney general nominee Todd Blanche promises to restrict abortion access, but how would he do that?

And the White House slams Tucker Carlson's "America first" moment as a whiny turncoat. But could Carlson actually run for president?

TUCKER CARLSON, FORMER FOX NEWS HOST: So probably going to go third party or multiple parties. Is that the best system? I don't know. It's better than the one we have

EL-SAYED: We don't need worry. We need work. So, if you're worried right now, get to work. That's the work that we need to do. And I can tell you on our campaign, we're going to be out there

knocking doors, having those conversations that are what our democracy is about. But worrying and Democrats worrying is not going to solve the problem.

CORNISH: Hey, Abdul El-Sayed ready to put in the work, with just 13 weeks left in the run-up to election day. Can he get his own party to unify around him?

Good morning, everybody. I'm Audie Cornish, and here is where we begin: that win for the Democrats' far-left-wing.

Abdul El-Sayed taking a victory lap Wednesday. Some key Democrats are still unconvinced. And senators and Dems admit that El-Sayed may have a tough road ahead.

SEN. GARY PETERS (D-MI): We have to win Michigan. It's absolutely essential for us to -- to keep that state blue, my state blue, and so that we can take the majority here in the U.S. Senate.

So, he's going to work hard, and we're going to now unite the party behind him.

I think he just needs to start reaching out to folks, which I'm sure he will, and that has to start immediately.

CORNISH: As for Republicans, President Trump thinks this is good news for his candidate, Mike Rogers.

DONALD TRUMP, U.S. PRESIDENT: Abdul El-Sayed, a lovely gentleman. He's a man of hate. And now he's going around saying, no, I love everybody. I love -- He doesn't love everybody. Put him in office. You're going to find out what he loves.

He doesn't love Israel. He doesn't love Jewish people. He hates them. He hates them with a passion that burns in his heart. And there's not a freaking thing he can do about it.

He won. And so, I think I'm happy.

CORNISH: All right. Joining me now in the group chat, some new faces: Stephen Neukam, congressional reporter for "NOTUS"; Doug Heye, Republican strategist and former RNC communications director; and Josh Orton, president for Demand Justice.

So, I want to start with my Demand Justice friend. Are people feeling like this is their moment? Did this feel like a turning point for this network of folks that has been outside of the Democratic Party and finding themselves winning in primaries?

JOSH ORTON, PRESIDENT, DEMAND JUSTICE: I mean, I think this is one of the biggest upsets in modern American political history.

He was outspent, you know, almost 10 to 1. There was $60 million of outside money.

He came -- Abdul came with a really strong argument against, you know, this power dynamic that's sort of crushing working people. You know, data centers being built in people's backyards. You know, the rising prices.

And I feel like he had a theory of that power and how he was going to fight it. And I think that is resonating.

And I think, frankly, people are making a mistake if they see this in too-partisan terms. He's talking about how people are being hurt by the current economy, by the tariffs that Trump has initiated.

And I think that is actually resonating with -- with Michigan. And this notion that somehow he's going to be a much harder sell in the general election, I don't think is necessarily true. He's an excellent political athlete. He lights up a room. He's optimistic and --

CORNISH: I like the term "political athlete." Right? Retail politics is real, I get that.

I want to be clear. Haley Stevens did perform well. Like, if you actually look at the state, it's not like he ran away with it. What was it, like, 15,000 votes? Oh, we got a little map. OK. The dark blue is El-Sayed.

So, I understand population centers, but just to be clear, those are a lot of rural areas, some black-leaning districts where he is going to have some work to do.

And here is how the first attack ad is going to look. I want you guys to take a listen.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, the most radical Senate candidate in America.

EL-SAYED: I'm pretty damn dangerous.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: El-Sayed pledged support for the leader of the Muslim Brotherhood, a designated foreign terrorist group. When his ally claimed America deserved 9/11 --

HASAN PIKER, TWITCH STREAMER: America deserved 9/11, dude.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: -- El-Sayed refused to disavow him.

EL-SAYED: I'm not here to disavow people's views.

CORNISH: It's interesting, that part about disavowing people's views because of the far-left podcaster, Hasan Piker, has been campaigning, you know, shoulder-to-shoulder with this guy.

And so, it's a little bit different than saying, oh, there's some people who have supported you in the distance. This is somebody who he is attached to, for better or worse, at this point.

STEPHEN NEUKAM, CONGRESSIONAL REPORTER, "NOTUS": Yes, absolutely. I also think that, look, there's going to be a lot that needs to be done to repair the party in Michigan after this primary. I mean, it was pretty nasty.

I mean, if you go back six years ago, seven years ago, Abdul lost to -- I'm sorry to now-Governor Whitmer by a landslide in that state. And this is a comeback story, seven years later, that has splintered the Democratic Party. Gary Peters, who you saw on the television just now, who used to be the -- the Democrat who ran campaigns for Senate Democrats, came out and endorsed Haley Stevens after saying he would not endorse in that race. The establishment put all their weight behind trying to crush Abdul in Michigan.

And, you know, the election shows that it didn't work. And there's going to have to be a lot of -- of repairing of feelings that -- that happens on the back end here.

CORNISH: Here's what Hasan Piker thinks of this idea of the repairing, and the mending, and all the language that you're supposed to use after a primary to bring everybody together. It sounded like this.

PIKER: Everyone being like, Abdul has a (EXPLETIVE DELETED) ton of work to do mending bridges. Here's a (EXPLETIVE DELETED) technique (ph) for you. OK?

You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of (EXPLETIVE DELETED). OK? You literally called the dude a (EXPLETIVE DELETED) terrorist for months on end and, like, called him a sexist, misogynist terrorist, bad candidate, doesn't -- fake doctor when he has, like, two (EXPLETIVE DELETED) degrees.

And now you're going to sit there and be like, well, you know, you've really got to come to me now. Like, what are you talking about? Do you want to (EXPLETIVE DELETED) win or not? Lock the (EXPLETIVE DELETED) in? OK.

CORNISH: Doug, what have Republicans learned from bear-hugging the independent podcast universe? DOUG HEYE, REPUBLICAN STRATEGIST: Look, I think --

CORNISH: It has implications towards the end of the show when we talk about Tucker Carlson and Megyn Kelly.

HEYE: Thanks for that.

CORNISH: I just wanted to let you know, so it's no spoiler.

HEYE: Look, I think those people that you embrace and you campaign with can help define your campaign. They can do it in good ways. They can do it in bad ways.

HEYE: When you come out of a victory -- you know, I watched the interview with -- with El-Sayed last night with Kaitlan Collins. He said and did all the right things.

The problem is his own people aren't helping him. That is as unhelpful as possible.

But I will say in sort of Piker's defense.

CORNISH: Yes, please.

HEYE: You know, so often when we talk about race and religion, we hear the term, especially about Republicans, "dog whistles" and "code words."

"AIPAC" has been a code word. It has been a dog whistle. And that word is "Jewish." It has attack the Jews, and so many candidates and campaigns have run with code words attacking Jews.

When -- when -- now I'm blanking on his name. Graham Platner from Maine. When he stepped out of his race, what did he do? He blamed AIPAC.

HEYE: Meaning he blamed the Jews. So --

CORNISH: And Thomas Massie --

HEYE: Piker is being --

CORNISH: -- protecting (ph) of his losses.

HEYE: And Piker is being blatantly obvious here and blatantly honest. And that is going to be a big part of this campaign, especially as there are repairs that have to be done.

I think we tend to oversell how divisive primaries are.

HEYE: Parties always come together. I remember Rachel Maddow telling me she would buy me a beer -- she said this on television -- if Rand Paul and Mitch McConnell had a unity event after their primary.

I texted her producer as soon as that segment was over and said, that event will be on Saturday afternoon. And I look forward. And by the way, Rachel made good on her promise.

But this kind of rhetoric coming from your supporters, who he was just with two days earlier, really not helpful.

CORNISH: Well, we have many weeks to go. So, obviously, we're going to talk about this a lot.

But coming up on CNN, in a matter of just hours, Anthony Fauci could be held in contempt, talking about Congress. And is this setting a dangerous precedent?

Plus, a new report showing Trump's immigration crackdown impacts military families and active-duty troops.

And then there's this.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Hopefully, there's somebody that the committee can find that -- that would be honest.

CORNISH: Chuck Edwards drops out of the race. So, who will Republicans find to replace him?

CORNISH: All right. It is now 13 minutes past the hour. Here are five things making the news this morning.

Iran reporting progress in talks with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, saying that the two sides are close to finalizing a proposed framework.

Now, Iran's foreign minister is saying that they have now agreed on a proposed safe shipping route, and a senior gulf official is saying that there's a 50-50 chance Iran and Oman will reach a deal by Friday.

J.D. VANCE, U.S. VICE PRESIDENT: We're kind of in the middle of the game, and I think people are trying to -- to prejudge exactly how this is going to go. I can tell you with confidence it's going to go in a place that is good for the United States of America, but we're going to use all the tools that we have -- military, economic, diplomatic -- to make sure we bring this thing to the right resolution.

CORNISH: The thing is, Iran insists that the talks are with Oman. These are bilateral talks. They deny negotiations with the U.S.

And the Trump administration has detained more than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty U.S. troops while pursuing their mass deportation agenda. That's according to an Associated Press investigation.

And at least six of them have been deported, and eight others remain in federal immigration custody.

And Republican leaders in Western North Carolina are going to meet next week to choose a replacement for Congressman Chuck Edwards. This is for the November ballot.

Edwards abandoned his reelection bid this week after an ethics panel found that he repeatedly made unwanted advances towards two female staffers. Here's one North Carolina voter.

UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I can probably count on my right hand how many honest people they are in Washington right now, and I've got one finger missing. Hopefully, there's somebody that the committee can find that that would be honest. That's my big thing. Honesty.

CORNISH: In the meantime, Edwards plans to serve out the remainder of his term.

And another day, another A.I. model has now apparently gone rogue. Meta this time announced this week that a model escaped onto the Internet and hacked into another company's system.
